questions.q: Pandit Omkar Nath Thakur was a student of .
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Pandit Vishnu Digambar Paluskar.

Key Points

• Pandit Vishnu Digambar Paluskar was one of the foremost figures in the revival of Hindustani classical music in the early 20th century.

• He founded the Gandharva Mahavidyalaya in 1901, which was instrumental in the democratization of classical music education.

• Pandit Omkar Nath Thakur was deeply influenced by Paluskar's teachings and philosophy of music.

• Paluskar's efforts were significant in promoting classical music among the masses and establishing structured music education in India.

Additional Information

• Pandit Vishnu Digambar Paluskar

• He was born on August 18, 1872, in Kurundwad, Maharashtra.

• He was a renowned Hindustani classical musician and is credited with creating a structured system of music education.

• Paluskar's efforts led to the founding of several music schools across India, ensuring the spread of classical music education.

• He composed many bhajans and patriotic songs, the most famous being "Raghupati Raghav Raja Ram".

• Gandharva Mahavidyalaya

• Established by Paluskar in 1901 in Lahore (now in Pakistan), it was the first institution to provide formal training in Hindustani classical music.

• The institution has branches all over India and continues to be a significant center for music education.

• Gandharva Mahavidyalaya’s curriculum blends traditional gurukul methods with modern educational techniques.

• Hindustani Classical Music

• It is one of the two main subgenres of Indian classical music, the other being Carnatic music.

• It originated in the northern part of India and encompasses a wide range of vocal and instrumental styles.

• Key features include ragas (melodic frameworks) and talas (rhythmic cycles).

• Music Education in India

• Formal music education in India has a rich history, with traditional gurukul systems being the earliest form of structured training.

• Modern institutions like Gandharva Mahavidyalaya and the Bhatkhande Music Institute have played crucial roles in popularizing classical music education.

• These institutions have produced many renowned musicians and have contributed significantly to the preservation and promotion of Indian classical music.

questions.q: As per a report of the Ministry of Labour and Employment, what was the rate of unemployment in Maharashtra for the year 2021-22?

• A lower unemployment rate typically indicates better economic conditions and higher employment levels.

Additional Information

• Unemployment Rate:

• It is the percentage of the labor force that is jobless and actively seeking employment.

• The formula for calculating the unemployment rate is: (Number of Unemployed / Labor Force) x 100.

• It is a key indicator used to measure the economic health of a region.

• High unemployment rates may indicate economic distress, while low rates may suggest a healthy economy.

• Ministry of Labour and Employment:

• It aims to create a healthy work environment for higher production and productivity and to develop and coordinate vocational skill training and employment services.

• Economic indicators are statistics that provide information about the economic performance of a country and its economic health.

• Common indicators include GDP, unemployment rates, inflation rates, and consumer price indices.

• Policymakers, economists, and analysts use these indicators to understand the current state of the economy and to guide economic policy decisions.

questions.q: Which of the following Articles states that the Prime Minister should be appointed by the President?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Article 75.

Key Points

• Article 75 of the Indian Constitution deals with the appointment of the Prime Minister and other ministers by the President.

• It states that the Prime Minister shall be appointed by the President and the other Ministers shall be appointed by the President on the advice of the Prime Minister.

• The article also discusses the collective responsibility of the Council of Ministers to the House of the People (Lok Sabha).

• It mentions that the Ministers shall hold office during the pleasure of the President.

Additional Information

• Article 62

• Article 62 deals with the time of holding election to fill a vacancy in the office of President and the term of office of the elected person.

• It specifies that an election to fill the vacancy caused by the expiration of the term of office of President shall be completed before the expiration of the term.

• It also states that an election to fill a vacancy in the office of President occurring by reason of his death, resignation, or removal, or otherwise, shall be held as soon as possible after, and in no case later than six months from, the date of occurrence of the vacancy.

• Article 66

• Article 66 deals with the election of the Vice-President of India.

• The Vice-President is elected by the members of an electoral college consisting of the members of both Houses of Parliament.

• The election is held in accordance with the system of proportional representation by means of the single transferable vote and the voting is by secret ballot.

• Article 71

• Article 71 deals with matters relating to, or connected with, the election of a President or Vice-President.

• It states that all doubts and disputes arising out of or in connection with the election of a President or Vice-President shall be inquired into and decided by the Supreme Court whose decision shall be final.

questions.q: Which two organic chemists are known for observing the peroxide effect in adding reagents to unsaturated compounds in 1933?
options: Morris S Kharasch and Frank R Mayo
C John Cadogen and Luis M Campos
B Steven Bachrach and Roald Hoffmann
Justus von Liebig and Friedrich Wöhler
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Morris S Kharasch and Frank R Mayo.

Key Points

• Morris S Kharasch and Frank R Mayo are known for their pioneering work in organic chemistry, particularly in the study of the peroxide effect.

• They observed the peroxide effect in 1933, which is also known as the Kharasch effect.

• This effect involves the addition of reagents to unsaturated compounds in the presence of peroxides, which leads to anti-Markovnikov addition.

• The discovery of the peroxide effect has had significant implications for synthetic organic chemistry, enabling the development of new reactions and synthetic pathways.

Additional Information

• Peroxide Effect (Kharasch Effect)

• This effect refers to the anti-Markovnikov addition of hydrogen bromide (HBr) to alkenes in the presence of peroxides.

• In the absence of peroxides, HBr adds to alkenes according to Markovnikov's rule, where the hydrogen attaches to the carbon with the greater number of hydrogen atoms.

• However, in the presence of peroxides, the addition follows the anti-Markovnikov rule, where the hydrogen attaches to the carbon with fewer hydrogen atoms.

• This phenomenon is due to the formation of free radicals initiated by the decomposition of peroxides.

• Free Radical Mechanism

• The peroxide effect proceeds through a free radical mechanism, which involves three main steps: initiation, propagation, and termination.

• Initiation: Peroxides decompose to form free radicals.

• Propagation: The free radicals react with HBr to generate bromine radicals, which then add to the alkene, forming new free radicals.

• Termination: The free radicals combine to form stable products, terminating the chain reaction.

• Importance in Organic Synthesis

• The peroxide effect is utilized in various synthetic applications, allowing chemists to control the regiochemistry of addition reactions.

• It has paved the way for the development of new reactions and methodologies in organic synthesis.

questions.q: What is the other name of tetanus caused by toxin producing bacteria called clostridium tetani?

• Lockjaw is a common name for tetanus, a serious bacterial infection.

• Tetanus is caused by the bacterium Clostridium tetani, which produces a toxin affecting the nervous system.

• The condition is characterized by muscle stiffness and spasms, particularly in the jaw muscles, hence the name "lockjaw".

• Without treatment, tetanus can be fatal, but it is preventable through vaccination.

Additional Information

• Clostridium tetani:

• It is a spore-forming bacterium found in soil, dust, and animal feces.

• The spores can enter the body through wounds, especially deep puncture wounds, and produce a toxin called tetanospasmin.

• Tetanospasmin interferes with the nervous system, leading to severe muscle spasms.

• Tetanus Symptoms:

• Symptoms typically appear 3 to 21 days after infection.

• Common symptoms include muscle stiffness, difficulty swallowing, and jaw cramping (lockjaw).

• Severe cases can lead to muscle spasms in the back, neck, and other parts of the body.

• Tetanus Treatment:

• Treatment usually involves wound care, medications to control muscle spasms, and antibiotics to fight the infection.

• In severe cases, patients may require hospitalization and supportive care, including mechanical ventilation.

• Tetanus Prevention:

• The best way to prevent tetanus is through vaccination.

• The DTaP (diphtheria, tetanus, and acellular pertussis) vaccine is routinely given to children, and booster shots (Td or Tdap) are recommended for adults every 10 years.

• Proper wound care and hygiene can also help prevent tetanus infection.

questions.q: WXYZ is a quadrilateral in which XQ and ZP are perpendicular to WY such that XQ = ZP. Diagonals ZX and WY intersect each other at point O. If OX = 12 cm, then find the value of ZX (in cm).
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

When perpendiculars drawn from opposite vertices of a quadrilateral to a diagonal are equal, that diagonal bisects the other diagonal.

Therefore, diagonal WY bisects diagonal ZX at intersection point O.

This directly means OX = OZ.

Given OX = 12 cm, the full length is ZX = 2 × OX.

⇒ ZX = 2 × 12 = 24 cm.

∴ The correct answer is 24 cm.

Alternate Method

• W Y X Z Q P O 12 cm

Given:

⇒ WXYZ is a quadrilateral with diagonal WY.

⇒ XQ ⊥ WY and ZP ⊥ WY.

⇒ XQ = ZP

⇒ OX = 12 cm

Method Used:

In ▵OXQ and ▵OZP:

⇒ ∠XQO = ∠ZPO = 90° (Given perpendiculars)

⇒ ∠XOQ = ∠ZOP (Vertically opposite angles are equal)

⇒ XQ = ZP (Given equal lengths)

⇒ ∴ ▵OXQ ≅ ▵OZP (By AAS congruence criterion)

Calculations:

⇒ Since ▵OXQ ≅ ▵OZP, their corresponding parts are equal.

⇒ OX = OZ (By CPCT - Corresponding Parts of Congruent Triangles)

⇒ Since OX = 12 cm, we have OZ = 12 cm.

⇒ The total length of diagonal ZX = OX + OZ

⇒ ZX = 12 + 12 = 24 cm.

∴ The correct answer is 24 cm.

Additional Information

AAS Congruence Rule

If any two angles and a non-included side of one triangle are equal to the corresponding angles and side of another triangle, the two triangles are congruent.

Area of Quadrilateral Property

If perpendiculars drawn from opposite vertices to a diagonal are equal in length, the diagonal divides the entire quadrilateral into two regions of exactly equal area.

Properties of Diagonals

Whenever a diagonal line of a quadrilateral divides the other diagonal into two equal halves, it must pass strictly through the midpoint of that second diagonal.

questions.q: The value of the expression sin x + cosec x = 2, then the value of sin⁷ x + cosec⁷ x is:
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

If x + 1/x = 2, then x = 1.

Here, sin x and cosec x are reciprocals of each other.

So, sin x + 1/(sin x) = 2 ⇒ sin x = 1 and cosec x = 1.

Then, sin⁷ x + cosec⁷ x = 1⁷ + 1⁷ = 1 + 1 = 2.

∴ The correct answer is 2.

Alternate Method

Given:

sin x + cosec x = 2

Formula Used:

cosec x = 1 / sin x

Calculations:

⇒ sin x + 1 / sin x = 2

⇒ (sin² x + 1) / sin x = 2

⇒ sin² x + 1 = 2 sin x

⇒ sin² x − 2 sin x + 1 = 0

⇒ (sin x − 1)² = 0

⇒ sin x = 1

Since cosec x is the reciprocal of sin x:

⇒ cosec x = 1 / 1 = 1

Now, substituting the values in the required expression:

⇒ sin⁷ x + cosec⁷ x = (1)⁷ + (1)⁷

⇒ 1 + 1 = 2

∴ The correct answer is 2.

Additional Information

Algebraic Identity of Reciprocals

If x + 1/x = 2, then x must be equal to 1. This is a standard result derived from the perfect square (x − 1)² = 0.

Negative Reciprocal Sum

If x + 1/x = −2, then x must be equal to −1. Substituting this value helps evaluate higher powers without expanding.

Trigonometric Reciprocal Pairs

The pairs (sin x, cosec x), (cos x, sec x), and (tan x, cot x) are reciprocals. If the sum of any pair is 2, the individual value of each function is exactly 1.

questions.q: In a family, the combined age of husband, wife and a son is 90 years. The husband is the oldest. The difference in the ages of the husband and wife is 31​rd the age of their son. After 10 years, the age of the son would be half the age of his father. What is the present age of his mother (in years)?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Let the Son's present age be S. From the condition 10 years later, Father's present age H = 2S + 10.

From the age difference, Mother's present age W = H − S/3 = (2S + 10) − S/3 = 5S/3 + 10.

Sum of all ages is 90: (2S + 10) + (5S/3 + 10) + S = 90

⇒ 3S + 5S/3 + 20 = 90

⇒ 14S/3 = 70 ⇒ S = 15

Mother's present age = (5 × 15)/3 + 10 = 25 + 10 = 35 years.

∴ The correct answer is 35 years.

Alternate Method

Given:

Present sum of ages: H + W + S = 90

Difference between Husband and Wife: H − W = S / 3

After 10 years: S + 10 = (H + 10) / 2



Calculations:

⇒ From the future age relation, 2S + 20 = H + 10

⇒ H = 2S + 10

⇒ Substituting H into the difference equation:

⇒ W = H − S / 3

⇒ W = (2S + 10) − S / 3 = (5S / 3) + 10

⇒ Substituting H and W into the sum equation:

⇒ (2S + 10) + ((5S / 3) + 10) + S = 90

⇒ 3S + 5S / 3 + 20 = 90

⇒ 14S / 3 = 70

⇒ S = 70 × 3 ÷ 14 = 15 years

⇒ The mother's present age W = (5 × 15 / 3) + 10

⇒ W = 25 + 10 = 35 years

∴ The correct answer is 35 years.

Additional Information

Problems on Ages

If the current age is x, then the age after 'n' years will be (x + n), and the age 'n' years ago was (x − n).

Constant Age Difference

The absolute age difference between any two individuals remains constant throughout their lives, irrespective of the time period.

Ratio of Ages

When solving problems based on changing ratios over time, it is highly useful to equate the differences in their respective ratios, because the actual difference in their ages never changes.

questions.q: What number should be subtracted from x³ - 4x² - 8x + 11 to make the number divisible by (x + 2)?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

By the Remainder Theorem, the required number to be subtracted is simply the remainder when the polynomial is divided by (x + 2).

Substitute x = −2 directly into the given expression:

Remainder = (−2)³ − 4(−2)² − 8(−2) + 11

Remainder = −8 − 16 + 16 + 11 = 3

∴ The correct answer is 3.

Alternate Method

Given:

Polynomial P(x) = x³ − 4x² − 8x + 11

Divisor = (x + 2)

Formula Used:

For a polynomial to be exactly divisible by (x + a), the remainder P(−a) must be zero. If we subtract the remainder from the polynomial, it becomes perfectly divisible.

Calculations:

⇒ Let the number to be subtracted be k.

⇒ Modified polynomial = x³ − 4x² − 8x + 11 − k

⇒ For perfect divisibility by (x + 2), substitute x = −2 and equate to zero.

⇒ (−2)³ − 4(−2)² − 8(−2) + 11 − k = 0

⇒ −8 − 4(4) + 16 + 11 − k = 0

⇒ −8 − 16 + 16 + 11 − k = 0

⇒ −8 + 11 − k = 0

⇒ 3 − k = 0

⇒ k = 3

∴ The correct answer is 3.

Additional Information

Remainder Theorem

If a polynomial P(x) is divided by a linear expression (x − a), the remainder is equal to P(a).

Factor Theorem

A polynomial P(x) has a factor (x − a) if and only if P(a) = 0. It is a specific condition of the Remainder Theorem where the remainder is zero.

Division Algorithm for Polynomials

Dividend = (Divisor × Quotient) + Remainder. If the remainder is subtracted from the dividend, the resulting polynomial is perfectly divisible by the divisor.

questions.q: If sinA + cosA = √3, then find the value of tanA + cotA + 2sinA.cosA.
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Squaring the given equation sinA + cosA = √3 yields 1 + 2sinAcosA = 3, which gives sinAcosA = 1.

The expression tanA + cotA simplifies directly to 1 / (sinAcosA).

Thus, the given expression becomes 1 / (sinAcosA) + 2sinAcosA.

Substituting sinAcosA = 1 gives 1 / 1 + 2 × 1 = 3.

∴ The correct answer is 3.

Alternate Method

Given:

sinA + cosA = √3

Formula Used:

(a + b)² = a² + b² + 2ab

sin²A + cos²A = 1

tanA = sinA / cosA

cotA = cosA / sinA

Calculations:

⇒ Squaring both sides of the given equation:

⇒ (sinA + cosA)² = (√3)²

⇒ sin²A + cos²A + 2sinAcosA = 3

⇒ 1 + 2sinAcosA = 3

⇒ 2sinAcosA = 3 − 1

⇒ 2sinAcosA = 2

⇒ sinAcosA = 1

Now, evaluating the required expression:

⇒ tanA + cotA + 2sinAcosA

⇒ (sinA / cosA) + (cosA / sinA) + 2sinAcosA

⇒ [(sin²A + cos²A) / (sinAcosA)] + 2sinAcosA

⇒ 1 / (sinAcosA) + 2sinAcosA

Substitute the value of sinAcosA = 1 into the expression:

⇒ 1 / 1 + 2 × 1

⇒ 1 + 2 = 3

∴ The correct answer is 3.

Additional Information

Basic Trigonometric Identities

sin²θ + cos²θ = 1

sec²θ − tan²θ = 1

cosec²θ − cot²θ = 1

tanθ + cotθ can always be simplified directly as: (sinθ / cosθ) + (cosθ / sinθ) = (sin²θ + cos²θ) / (sinθcosθ) = 1 / (sinθcosθ).

questions.q: The cost of a diamond varies directly as the square of its weight. Once, this diamond broke into four pieces with weights in the ratio of 4 : 3 : 2 : 1 .When the pieces were sold, the merchant got ₹63,000 less than that of one piece. Find the original price of the diamond.
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Total weight = 4 + 3 + 2 + 1 = 10 parts, so Original price ∝ (10)² = 100 parts.

New total price ∝ 4² + 3² + 2² + 1² = 16 + 9 + 4 + 1 = 30 parts.

Loss in value = 100 parts − 30 parts = 70 parts.

70 parts = ₹63,000 ⇒ 1 part = ₹900.

Original price = 100 parts × ₹900 = ₹90,000.

∴ The correct answer is ₹90,000.

Alternate Method

Given:

Weight ratio of the four broken pieces = 4 : 3 : 2 : 1

Loss after selling the pieces = ₹63,000

Formula Used:

Cost (C) ∝ Weight (W)² ⇒ C = kW²

Calculations:



⇒ Let the weights of the broken pieces be 4x, 3x, 2x, and 1x.

⇒ Total weight of the original diamond = 4x + 3x + 2x + 1x = 10x

⇒ Original cost of the diamond = k(10x)² = 100kx²

⇒ Cost of the broken pieces = k(4x)² + k(3x)² + k(2x)² + k(x)²

⇒ Total cost of the pieces = 16kx² + 9kx² + 4kx² + 1kx² = 30kx²

⇒ Loss incurred = Original Cost − Total cost of pieces

⇒ Loss = 100kx² − 30kx² = 70kx²

⇒ Given that the loss is ₹63,000:

⇒ 70kx² = 63000

⇒ kx² = 63000 ÷ 70 = 900

⇒ Original Cost = 100kx² = 100 × 900 = 90,000

∴ The correct answer is ₹90,000.

Additional Information

Direct Proportion

When a quantity varies directly as the square of another, the relation is given by y = kx². A proportional increase in x causes a quadratic increase in y.

Loss on Breakage

For any item whose value is proportional to the square of its weight, breaking it into smaller parts will strictly decrease its total value because (a + b)² > a² + b² for any positive weights.

Ratio Distribution

If an amount is divided in the ratio a : b : c, the parts can be expressed as ax, bx, and cx where x is a common variable. The sum of the parts always equals the original amount.

questions.q: A vendor started selling vegetables at ₹10 per kg, but couldn’t find buyers at this rate. So he reduced the price to ₹7.2 per kg, but uses a faulty weight of 900 g instead of 1 kg. Find the percentage change in the actual price.
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Initial actual price of vegetables = ₹10 per kg

New actual price for 1000 g = (₹7.2 ÷ 900) × 1000 = ₹8 per kg

Percentage change = [(Initial price − New price) ÷ Initial price] × 100

Percentage change = [(10 − 8) ÷ 10] × 100 = 20%

∴ The correct answer is 20%.

Alternate Method

Given:

Initial price of vegetables = ₹10 per kg (1000 g)

New claimed selling price = ₹7.2 for a faulty weight of 900 g

Formula Used:

Actual price per kg = (Selling Price ÷ Faulty Weight) × 1000

Percentage Change = [(Initial Price − Actual New Price) ÷ Initial Price] × 100



Calculations:

⇒ Actual new price for 1000 g = (7.2 ÷ 900) × 1000

⇒ Actual new price = 0.008 × 1000 = ₹8 per kg

⇒ Decrease in price per kg = Initial Price − Actual New Price

⇒ Decrease = 10 − 8 = ₹2

⇒ Percentage change = (2 ÷ 10) × 100

⇒ Percentage change = 20%

∴ The correct answer is 20%.

Additional Information

Dishonest Dealer Concept

When a dealer claims to sell goods at cost price but uses a false weight, his profit percentage is given by [(True Weight − False Weight) ÷ False Weight] × 100.

Effective Price Standardization

Always standardize quantities (e.g., to 1 kg or 1000 g) before comparing prices or calculating profit/loss percentages to avoid calculation errors.

Percentage Change Formula

The general formula for percentage change is [(Final Value − Initial Value) ÷ Initial Value] × 100. A negative result indicates a decrease.

questions.q: The cost of tomatoes per kg is increased by 300%. A housewife reduces her consumption of tomatoes by 70%. By what percentage does her expenditure on tomatoes increase or decrease?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

The net percentage change in expenditure can be found using the successive percentage formula: x + y + (x × y) ÷ 100

Here, the price increases by 300% (x = +300) and consumption decreases by 70% (y = −70).

Net change = 300 − 70 + [300 × (−70)] ÷ 100

Net change = 230 − 210 = +20%

Since the result is positive, the expenditure increases by 20%.

∴ The correct answer is Increases, 20%.

Alternate Method

Given:

Percentage increase in price = 300%

Percentage decrease in consumption = 70%

Formula Used:

Expenditure = Price × Consumption



Calculations:

⇒ Let the initial price of tomatoes be ₹100 per kg and the initial consumption be 10 kg.

⇒ Initial Expenditure = 100 × 10 = ₹1000

⇒ New price after 300% increase = 100 + (300 ÷ 100) × 100 = ₹400 per kg

⇒ New consumption after 70% decrease = 10 − (70 ÷ 100) × 10 = 3 kg

⇒ New Expenditure = 400 × 3 = ₹1200

⇒ Change in Expenditure = 1200 − 1000 = ₹200 (Increase)

⇒ Percentage Increase = (200 ÷ 1000) × 100 = 20%

∴ The correct answer is Increases, 20%.

Additional Information

Successive Percentage Change

When a quantity is successively changed by x% and y%, the net percentage change is given by the formula: x + y + (x × y) ÷ 100. Use positive values for an increase and negative values for a decrease.

Price, Consumption, and Expenditure Relation

The foundational rule is Expenditure = Price × Consumption. If expenditure needs to remain constant while the price increases, consumption must be decreased proportionately.

Fraction Equivalent Method

For compound percentage calculations, converting percentages to fractional multipliers simplifies multiplication. For example, a 300% increase means multiplying the base value by 4, and a 70% decrease means multiplying the base value by 3/10.

Rate of interest for Scheme B = 5% p.a., Time = 7 years

Total interest received = ₹1,620

Formula Used:

Simple Interest (SI) = (P × R × T) ÷ 100



Calculations:

⇒ 1.8P = 1620

⇒ P = 1620 ÷ 1.8 = 900

⇒ Amount invested in Scheme B = 4P = 4 × 900 = 3600

∴ The correct answer is ₹3,600.

Additional Information

Effective Interest Rate in SI

Total Amount in Simple Interest

Simple Interest vs Compound Interest

In SI, the interest is calculated only on the initial principal. In Compound Interest (CI), interest is calculated on the principal and also on the accumulated interest of previous periods.

questions.q: Two trains of lengths 150 m and 250 m run on parallel lines. When they run in the same direction, they take 20 seconds to cross each other and, when they run in the opposite direction, they take 5 seconds to cross each other. What is the speed of the two trains?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Total distance = 150 + 250 = 400 m.

Relative speed in same direction = S₁ − S₂ = 400 ÷ 20 = 20 m/s.

Relative speed in opposite direction = S₁ + S₂ = 400 ÷ 5 = 80 m/s.

Solving, S₁ = (80 + 20) ÷ 2 = 50 m/s and S₂ = (80 − 20) ÷ 2 = 30 m/s.

Speeds in km/h = 50 × (18/5) = 180 km/h and 30 × (18/5) = 108 km/h.

∴ The correct answer is 180 km/h and 108 km/h.

Alternate Method

Given:

Length of first train (L₁) = 150 m

Length of second train (L₂) = 250 m

Time taken to cross in same direction (T₁) = 20 seconds

Time taken to cross in opposite direction (T₂) = 5 seconds

Formula Used:

Speed = Distance ÷ Time

Total distance covered to cross each other = L₁ + L₂



Calculations:

⇒ Total Distance = 150 + 250 = 400 m

⇒ Let the speed of the first train be u m/s and the second train be v m/s.

⇒ When running in the same direction, relative speed = u − v

⇒ u − v = 400 ÷ 20 = 20 m/s ... (Equation 1)

⇒ When running in opposite directions, relative speed = u + v

⇒ u + v = 400 ÷ 5 = 80 m/s ... (Equation 2)

⇒ Adding Equation 1 and Equation 2:

⇒ 2u = 100 ⇒ u = 50 m/s

⇒ Subtracting Equation 1 from Equation 2:

⇒ 2v = 60 ⇒ v = 30 m/s

⇒ Convert speeds to km/h by multiplying with (18/5):

⇒ Speed of first train = 50 × (18/5) = 180 km/h

⇒ Speed of second train = 30 × (18/5) = 108 km/h

∴ The correct answer is 180 km/h and 108 km/h.

Additional Information

Relative Speed

When two objects move in opposite directions, their relative speed is the sum of their individual speeds (S₁ + S₂). When moving in the same direction, it is the difference of their speeds (|S₁ − S₂|).

Distance While Crossing

When two trains cross each other, the total distance covered is always the sum of their lengths (L₁ + L₂), regardless of the direction they are moving.

Unit Conversion Trick

To rapidly convert speed from m/s to km/h, multiply the value by 18/5. To convert from km/h to m/s, multiply by 5/18.

questions.q: ​Each of Ravi and Kavita had some marbles. Kavita had 12 more marbles than Ravi had. If each of them had one more marble, then three times the number of marbles Kavita had would be equal to four times the number of marbles Ravi had. How many marbles did Kavita actually have?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Since both persons receive 1 more marble, the difference in their marble count remains 12.

The new ratio of Kavita's to Ravi's marbles is derived from 3 × Kavita = 4 × Ravi, giving a ratio of 4 : 3.

The difference in ratio parts is 4 − 3 = 1 unit.

Since 1 unit = 12 marbles, Kavita's new marble count = 4 units = 48 marbles.

Kavita's actual marbles before the addition = 48 − 1 = 47 marbles.

∴ The correct answer is 47 marbles.

Alternate Method

Given:

Kavita had 12 more marbles than Ravi had.

If each of them gets 1 more marble, 3 × (Kavita's new marbles) = 4 × (Ravi's new marbles).



Calculations:

⇒ Let Ravi's actual marbles = R

⇒ Kavita's actual marbles = R + 12

⇒ When both get 1 more marble, the difference between their totals remains 12.

⇒ 3 × (New Kavita) = 4 × (New Ravi)

⇒ (New Kavita) / (New Ravi) = 4 / 3

⇒ Difference in ratio = 4 units − 3 units = 1 unit

⇒ 1 unit corresponds to the difference of 12 marbles.

⇒ Kavita's new marbles = 4 units = 4 × 12 = 48 marbles

⇒ Kavita's actual marbles = 48 − 1 = 47 marbles

∴ The correct answer is 47 marbles.

Additional Information

Constant Difference Rule

When the same uniform quantity is added to or subtracted from two numbers, the numerical difference between the two numbers remains completely unchanged.

Ratio Translation

A mathematical statement equating two products in the form "a × A = b × B" translates directly into the inverse ratio form A : B = b : a.

Direct Unitary Method

When a given quantitative value corresponds to a specific difference in ratio parts, 1 ratio unit can be calculated directly by dividing the actual difference by the ratio part difference.

questions.q: 15 kg of ₹10 per kg wheat is mixed with 5 kg of another type of wheat to get a mixture costing ₹30 per kg. Find the price (per kg) of the costlier wheat.
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

By the rule of alligation, the ratio of quantities equals the cross-difference of their unit prices.

Ratio of quantities given = 15 kg : 5 kg = 3 : 1

Using the alligation cross ratio ⇒ (x − 30) : (30 − 10) = 3 : 1

⇒ (x − 30) ÷ 20 = 3

⇒ x − 30 = 60 ⇒ x = 90

∴ The correct answer is ₹90.

Alternate Method

Given:

Quantity of cheaper wheat (Q₁) = 15 kg

Price of cheaper wheat (P₁) = ₹10 per kg

Quantity of costlier wheat (Q₂) = 5 kg

Average price of the mixture (Pₘ) = ₹30 per kg

Let the price of the costlier wheat be P₂ = ₹x per kg.

Formula Used:

Total cost of mixture = Sum of individual costs

⇒ Q₁ × P₁ + Q₂ × P₂ = (Q₁ + Q₂) × Pₘ



Calculation:

⇒ 15 × 10 + 5 × x = (15 + 5) × 30

⇒ 150 + 5x = 20 × 30

⇒ 150 + 5x = 600

⇒ 5x = 600 − 150

⇒ 5x = 450

⇒ x = 90

∴ The correct answer is ₹90.

Additional Information

Rule of Alligation

It gives the exact ratio in which two ingredients at different prices must be mixed to obtain a desired average mixture price. Formula: Q꜀ₕₑₐₚₑᵣ ÷ Q꜀ₒₛₜₗᵢₑᵣ = (P꜀ₒₛₜₗᵢₑᵣ − Pₘₑₐₙ) ÷ (Pₘₑₐₙ − P꜀ₕₑₐₚₑᵣ).

Weighted Average Method

The rule of alligation is practically a simplified cross-multiplication of the weighted average formula Pₘ = (Q₁P₁ + Q₂P₂) ÷ (Q₁ + Q₂).

Versatility of Alligation

The Alligation shortcut is not only restricted to price and mixture amounts; it is universally applicable across chapters like Speed & Distance, Percentages, Profit & Loss, and Averages.

questions.q: If 3sin²θ + 5cos²θ = 4 and θ is an acute angle, then the value of tanθ is:
options: 21​
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Divide the entire equation by cos²θ to get: 3tan²θ + 5 = 4sec²θ

Substitute sec²θ = 1 + tan²θ into the equation:

3tan²θ + 5 = 4(1 + tan²θ)

5 − 4 = 4tan²θ − 3tan²θ ⇒ tan²θ = 1

Since θ is an acute angle, tanθ = 1.

∴ The correct answer is 1.

Alternate Method

Given:

3sin²θ + 5cos²θ = 4

Formula Used:

sin²θ + cos²θ = 1

tanθ = Perpendicular ÷ Base

Calculations:



⇒ 3sin²θ + 3cos²θ + 2cos²θ = 4

⇒ 3(sin²θ + cos²θ) + 2cos²θ = 4

⇒ 3(1) + 2cos²θ = 4

⇒ 2cos²θ = 1

⇒ cos²θ = 1 / 2

⇒ cosθ = 1 / √2

⇒ Since θ is an acute angle, θ = 45°

⇒ tanθ = tan(45°) = 1

∴ The correct answer is 1.

Additional Information

Trigonometric Identities

Fundamental identities: sin²θ + cos²θ = 1, sec²θ − tan²θ = 1, and cosec²θ − cot²θ = 1.

Angles in the First Quadrant

For any acute angle (0° < θ < 90°), all six trigonometric ratios (sin, cos, tan, cot, sec, cosec) are positive.

Values at 45°

When θ = 45°, the perpendicular and base of a right triangle are equal in length, giving tan(45°) = 1 and sin(45°) = cos(45°) = 1/√2.

• Passive voice structure: The subject receives the action and is usually followed by the word "by" along with the doer of the action.

• In the given passive voice sentence, "Data is being collected by the researcher," the subject is "Data," and the doer is "the researcher."

• To convert to active voice, make "the researcher" the subject of the sentence and use the appropriate verb form.

• Active voice sentence: "The researcher is collecting data."

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Correct Sentence: *"The researcher is collecting data."*

Additional Information

• Option 1: "The researcher has collected data." – Incorrect as it changes the tense.

• Option 3: "The researcher has been collecting data." – Incorrect as it implies a different duration or continuity.

• Option 4: "The researcher will be collecting data." – Incorrect as it changes the tense to future.
